main.title: The Vietnam War ends
main.summary: The Vietnam War ended on April 30, 1975, after a conflict involving Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia that had intensified within the Cold War.

cards.heading: The Vietnam War ends
cards.text:
The Vietnam War ended on April 30, 1975. Fought from around 1955, it pitted North Vietnam and its allies against South Vietnam and its allies, with fighting extending into Laos and Cambodia. The Soviet Union and China supported the North, while the United States and other anti-communist countries supported the South.

The conflict combined struggles over national independence, a divided Vietnam and the international rivalries of the Cold War. Direct US military involvement escalated in 1965, and US forces withdrew in 1973. Fighting also contributed to the civil wars in Laos and Cambodia. All three countries had communist governments by the end of 1975.

main.title: One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest
main.subtitle: McMurphy challenges the routines of a hospital ward
main.summary: Miloš Forman's One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest brings Randle McMurphy into a psychiatric hospital whose routines are controlled by Nurse Ratched. Jack Nicholson and Louise Fletcher play the two figures around whom the ward's tensions gather. Adapted from Ken Kesey's novel, the film opened in New York and Los Angeles on 19 November 1975.

cards.heading: A new arrival on the ward
cards.text: Miloš Forman's One Flew Over the Cuckoo's Nest brings Randle McMurphy into a psychiatric hospital whose routines are controlled by Nurse Ratched. Jack Nicholson and Louise Fletcher play the two figures around whom the ward's tensions gather. Adapted from Ken Kesey's novel, the film opened in New York and Los Angeles on 19 November 1975.

cards.heading: Who decides the rules?
cards.text: McMurphy initially treats the hospital as a place he can manipulate, but his challenges to its rules begin to involve the other patients. Small arguments about schedules, games and permissions become tests of who may make decisions. Ratched's authority is expressed through meetings and apparently reasonable procedures, so the conflict often develops inside an ordinary conversation. The patients' different reactions give the group its character: a disruption that amuses one man can expose another to fear or punishment.

cards.heading: An ensemble inside the institution
cards.text: Forman filmed in an operating Oregon hospital, grounding much of the story in a real institutional setting. The ensemble gives each encounter a life beyond the two central performances, including Brad Dourif's Billy Bibbit and Will Sampson's Chief Bromden. At the 1976 Oscars, the film won best picture, director, actor, actress and adapted screenplay. Its concentration on behaviour, dependence and power makes the consequences of resistance felt through the people who must continue living together on the ward.

main.title: Apple I
main.summary: The Apple-1 is an 8-bit personal computer designed by Steve Wozniak and introduced by Apple Computer in 1976.

cards.heading: Apple I
cards.text:
The Apple-1 is an 8-bit personal computer designed by Steve Wozniak and introduced by Apple Computer in 1976. It was the company's first product. Steve Jobs, Wozniak's friend and Apple's co-founder, proposed founding the company and marketing the machine.

The Apple-1 arrived as a pre-assembled motherboard with built-in video terminal circuitry, allowing a direct connection to a household television through composite video. Buyers supplied their own case, power supply and keyboard. Its MOS Technology 6502 processor and integrated display circuitry made it one of the earliest personal computers, alongside the Sol-20, to offer these capabilities.

main.title: Rocky
main.summary: Rocky introduced Sylvester Stallone's Philadelphia boxer in 1976.

cards.heading: Rocky
cards.text: Rocky introduced Sylvester Stallone's Philadelphia boxer in 1976. A small-time fighter and debt collector, Rocky Balboa receives an unexpected chance to challenge heavyweight champion Apollo Creed. Stallone wrote the screenplay and insisted on playing the lead, rejecting an offer for the rights that would have excluded him from the role. John G. Avildsen directed the film on a budget of about one million dollars. Filming around Philadelphia connected its underdog story to recognisable streets and landmarks, including the steps that became associated with Rocky's preparation for the fight.

main.title: Taxi Driver
main.summary: Taxi Driver is a 1976 American neo-noir psychological drama film directed by Martin Scorsese and written by Paul Schrader.

cards.heading: Taxi Driver
cards.text:
Taxi Driver is a 1976 American neo-noir psychological drama film directed by Martin Scorsese and written by Paul Schrader. Set in New York City in a time of urban decay following the Vietnam War, it stars Robert De Niro as taxi driver Travis Bickle, whose mental state deteriorates as he works nights in the city, eventually having a mental breakdown and becoming a vigilante. The film also features Jodie Foster, Cybill Shepherd, Harvey Keitel, Peter Boyle, Leonard Harris and Albert Brooks (in his first feature film role).

Filming began in summer 1975, with actors taking pay cuts to ensure that the project could be completed on its low budget of $1.9 million ($11.4 million in 2025). For the score, Bernard Herrmann composed what would be his final score. The music was finished mere hours before his death, and the film is dedicated to him.

main.title: VHS
main.summary: VHS (Video Home System) is a discontinued standard for consumer-level analog video recording on tape cassettes, introduced on September 9, 1976 by the Victor Company of Japan (JVC, a subsidiary of Matsushita).

cards.heading: VHS
cards.text:
VHS (Video Home System) is a discontinued standard for consumer-level analog video recording on tape cassettes, introduced on September 9, 1976 by the Victor Company of Japan (JVC, a subsidiary of Matsushita). It was the dominant home video format throughout the tape media period of the 1980s and 1990s.

Magnetic tape video recording was adopted by the television industry in the 1950s in the form of the first commercialized video tape recorders (VTRs), but the devices were expensive and used only in professional environments. In the 1970s, videotape technology became affordable for home use, and widespread adoption of videocassette recorders (VCRs) began; the VHS became the most popular media format for VCRs as it would win the "format war" against Betamax (backed by Sony) and a number of other competing tape standards.

main.title: Apple II
main.summary: The Apple II went on sale on 10 June 1977, bringing Steve Wozniak's computer design into a complete plastic case with a keyboard and colour graphics.

cards.heading: Apple II
cards.text: The Apple II went on sale on 10 June 1977, bringing Steve Wozniak's computer design into a complete plastic case with a keyboard and colour graphics. Its open architecture allowed users and manufacturers to extend the machine. Alongside the Commodore PET and TRS-80, it helped establish the home computer market. Software widened its audience: the VisiCalc spreadsheet, released in 1979, gave businesses a practical reason to buy one. Schools and homes became important settings too. Successive models kept the Apple II family in production until 1993, with the IIe becoming its best-selling version.

main.title: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
main.summary: Steven Spielberg's Close Encounters of the Third Kind appeared in 1977, connecting several lives through unexplained encounters with visitors from space.

cards.heading: Close Encounters of the Third Kind
cards.text: Steven Spielberg's Close Encounters of the Third Kind appeared in 1977, connecting several lives through unexplained encounters with visitors from space. An Indiana worker becomes absorbed by what he has seen, a mother searches for her abducted child, and a French scientist investigates related events around the world. Their separate experiences give the mystery several human perspectives. Spielberg developed the project from an idea he had long wanted to film. Its title draws on astronomer J. Allen Hynek's classification, in which an encounter of the third kind involves observing extraterrestrial beings.

main.title: Commodore PET
main.summary: Commodore presented the PET at the Consumer Electronics Show in January 1977.

cards.heading: Commodore PET
cards.text: Commodore presented the PET at the Consumer Electronics Show in January 1977. Its single case combined a keyboard, monochrome monitor, MOS Technology 6502 processor and BASIC, with a cassette deck in early models. That integrated design offered a complete route into personal computing. Together with the Apple II and TRS-80, it helped establish a new market for ready-made machines. Later PET models gained memory, larger screens and improved keyboards. Schools in Canada and the United States became important customers, while European businesses also adopted the range.

main.title: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols
main.summary: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols (often shortened to Never Mind the Bollocks) is the only studio album by the English punk rock band the Sex Pistols.

cards.heading: Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols
cards.text:
Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols (often shortened to Never Mind the Bollocks) is the only studio album by the English punk rock band the Sex Pistols. It was released on 28 October 1977 through Virgin Records. As a result of the Sex Pistols' volatile internal relationships, the band's lineup saw changes during the recording of the album. Original bass guitarist Glen Matlock left the band early in the recording process. While he is credited as a co-writer on all but two of the tracks, Matlock played bass on only one track, "Anarchy in the U.K."

Recording sessions continued with a new bass player, Sid Vicious, who is credited on two of the songs written by the band after he joined. While Vicious's bass playing appeared on two tracks, his lack of skill on the instrument meant that many of the tracks were recorded with guitarist Steve Jones playing bass instead. Drummer Paul Cook, Jones and singer Johnny Rotten appear on every track.
